newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ to continue money policy for economic recovery.
newsitem.headline: BOJ to continue money policy for economic recovery.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Wednesday that the central bank will continue to conduct its monetary policy with the aim of strengthening the basis for Japan's economic recovery.
"For the time being we will continue to carry out monetary policy putting emphasis on strengthening the basis of the economic recovery," he told a news conference.
Matsushita said that the economy was being affected by the rise in Japan's consumption tax from April 1, but added that overall, it was continuing its gradual recovery.
He said housing spending remained weak due to the rise in the tax.
He also said that although there were signs of recovery, a fall in private consumption was seen in reaction to the tax increase.
But he said that, taking into account the recovery in jobs and incomes, the recovery trend in private spending was likely to continue.
The governor also said that capital spending remained strong and that Japan's net exports had been supporting the economic recovery since last autumn.
Matsushita said production was likely to experience a temporary setback in the April to June quarter.
However, due to improvements in personal incomes and corporate earnings, the economic recovery is highly likely to continue to overcome the negative effects of fiscal consolidation measures, he said.
Matsushita said domestic prices were likely to be stable for the time being, excluding the effect from the rise in the consumption tax.
